title: Yerba Buena Gardens expense claims led to a $400,000 settlement and contracting injunction

beats.text: A Gardens manager could bill a fee and claim direct operating expenses separately.

visual.sub: The manager earned a fee and could submit separate direct expenses

beats.text: The aggregate management fee cap was $1,393,889.

visual.label: The manager earned a fee and could submit separate direct expenses

beats.text: In 2020 the City and its redevelopment successor sued the manager.

visual.kicker: The City and its redevelopment successor alleged false expense claims

beats.text: Their allegations concerned reimbursements for property management expenses.

visual.kicker: The City and its redevelopment successor alleged false expense claims

beats.text: The City authorized a $400,000 settlement with MJM.

visual.label: The settlement authorized a recovery and a three-year contracting injunction

beats.text: The terms also called for a three-year injunction against future City contracts.

visual.kicker: The settlement authorized a recovery and a three-year contracting injunction

beats.text: The terms allocated shares to the private plaintiff and the City Attorney.

visual.kicker: The settlement authorized a recovery and a three-year contracting injunction

beats.text: The City share could support only the continued operation of the Gardens.

visual.kicker: The settlement authorized a recovery and a three-year contracting injunction

beats.text: Fourteen payment lines carried dates in 2023 or 2025.

visual.kicker: Later-looking payment labels required a supplier cross-check

beats.text: All fourteen said Direct Payments and belonged to earlier fiscal years.

visual.kicker: Later-looking payment labels required a supplier cross-check

beats.text: The same two contract numbers appeared across thousands of payees.
